title: 'Stop Being a Princess': Australian Fan Heckles Steve Smith Over Sightscreen Antics as Bangladesh Dominate in Darwin
excerpt: Smith scored a battling 71 but was called out by a frustrated spectator for repeatedly asking a cameraperson to move from the sightscreen as Australia collapsed to 198 all out.
body:
• An Australian fan yelled 'Stop being a princess' at Steve Smith after the batter repeatedly asked a cameraperson to move from the sightscreen during the Darwin Test
  • Smith scored a fighting 71 but was the lone resistance as Australia were bowled out for 198 against Bangladesh
  • Hasan Mahmud took career-best figures of 6-55, his third five-wicket haul, all taken away from home
  • Bangladesh finished the day at 96-1, with the match setting up for one of the most significant results in the team's Test history

Smith's Sightscreen Standoff

Former Australia captain Steve Smith found himself the target of crowd frustration during the opening day of the Darwin Test against Bangladesh, when an Australian fan shouted at him to "stop being a princess" after his repeated objections to a cameraperson positioned near the sightscreen.

Smith, batting in a lone hand while wickets fell around him, paused multiple times to gesture at the camera operator sitting at the base of the sightscreen. The delays visibly annoyed sections of the home crowd.

"Just hit the damn thing Smudge. Stop being a princess. You're not bigger than the game Stevie. Deal with it."

— Australian fan at the Darwin Test

The exchange, captured by broadcast microphones, quickly circulated on social media and drew mixed reactions — some backing Smith's right to an unobstructed view, others siding with the fan's bluntness, according to Wisden.

Bangladesh Bowl Australia Out for 198

The on-field drama overshadowed what was a difficult day for Australia. Smith walked in at 52-2 after Hasan Mahmud removed both openers, and was dropped just eight balls into his innings. He made the reprieve count, reaching a 45th Test fifty, but no other Australian batter managed to cross 25.

Mahmud was the chief destroyer, returning career-best figures of 6-55 — his third five-wicket haul in Tests, all of which have come away from home. Taskin Ahmed and Ebadot Hossain provided strong support, claiming two wickets each as Australia's batting lineup crumbled around Smith, according to Wisden.

Smith eventually became Mahmud's fifth victim, and Australia were bowled out for 198 — a well-below-par total on a Darwin pitch that offered assistance to Bangladesh's pace trio.

Bangladesh in the Box Seat

Bangladesh batters then capped off what Wisden described as "one of their greatest days of Test cricket" by reaching 96-1 at stumps, with Mominul Haque (35 not out) and Tanzid Hasan Tamim (32 not out) at the crease. The visitors trail by just 102 runs with nine wickets in hand.

This is Bangladesh's first Test in Australia in 23 years, and the performance signals a dramatic improvement in the team's fast bowling capabilities. Mahmud, Taskin, and Ebadot formed a pace attack that was disciplined, aggressive, and relentless throughout the day.

India Connection: What It Means for Asian Cricket

Bangladesh's dominance with the ball in Australian conditions carries significant implications for the broader Asian cricket landscape. Indian cricket fans will be watching this Test closely — Bangladesh's pace attack, which has troubled India in recent bilateral series, is proving it can compete in the toughest overseas conditions.

For Indian cricket followers in Australia and across the diaspora, the sight of an Asian pace attack dismantling Australia on home soil resonates deeply. India's own fast bowling revolution over the past decade, spearheaded by bowlers like Jasprit Bumrah and Mohammed Shami, opened the door for subcontinent teams to believe they could win in pace-friendly conditions. Bangladesh's performance in Darwin suggests that revolution is spreading.

Smith, who has been a familiar adversary for India across IPL seasons and bilateral series, continues to be a polarising figure. His sightscreen habits — well-known to Indian bowlers who have waited him out in the IPL — add another layer of intrigue to the cricketing storylines that connect India, Australia, and Bangladesh.

With the match finely poised, the remaining days in Darwin could produce a result that reshapes perceptions of Bangladesh cricket — and gives Asian cricket another milestone to celebrate.
